en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn to say how much of a quality something has, and what happens because of it: so hot, such a good film, too tired, old enough. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: so + a describing word
steps.text: You know very, really and quite. Let's start with a word that adds feeling: so.
steps.body:
**so** makes a word stronger, with feeling, like *banget*: *It's so hot today!* It goes before an **adjective** (a describing word: *hot, tired*) or an **adverb** (how: *fast, well*), with **no noun** after it.

Add **that** + what happened to show the **result** (*akibat*): *I was so tired that I fell asleep on the KRL.* Indonesian: *begitu … sehingga …*. This isn't *so* = *jadi* from linkers (*I was tired, so I went home*).

pairs.en: I was so tired that I fell asleep on the KRL.
pairs.id: Saya begitu capek sehingga tertidur di KRL.

steps.title: such + a noun phrase
steps.text: Now, what if a noun comes at the end?
steps.body:
If the phrase **ends with a noun** (a thing or person word: *film, beaches, weather*), use **such**. One countable thing → **such a/an**: *such a good film*. Plural or uncountable → **such** without a: *such long queues, such bad weather*.

Quick test: look at the **last word**. Describing word → **so**; noun → **such**. Not `so a good film`.

examples.en: It was such a good film!
Pak Hasan is such a patient boss.
examples.id: Pak Hasan atasan yang sabar sekali.
Bali punya pantai-pantai yang indah sekali.

examples.en: We had such bad weather in Puncak.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Sari's new colleagues help her every day. Look at the last word of the phrase.

question.explanation: The phrase ends with a noun (**people**), so use **such**. *people* is plural, so there's no *a*: **such nice people**. `so nice people` is wrong: so can't go before a noun phrase.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: There was a big storm in Bogor yesterday. Say what happened because of it.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Hujannya begitu deras sehingga kami tinggal di rumah.
question.solution: It rained so hard that we stayed home.
question.explanation: **so** + adverb (*rain hard* = hujan deras), then **that** + the result: *we stayed home*. *begitu … sehingga* = **so … that**.

steps.title: too = a problem
steps.text: Next: a word that always means there's a problem.
steps.body:
**too** = *terlalu*: more than is OK. *This shirt is too small* (I can't wear it). Add **to + verb** for what you can't do: *He's too young to vote*, or **for** + a person: *too expensive for me*.

Before an adjective it's just **too**, not `too much expensive`: **too much** goes before uncountable nouns (*too much sugar*).

Trap: *terlalu enak* can be praise in Indonesian, but English **too** never is. For praise use **so / really / very**.

pairs.en: It's very hot, but we can go out.
pairs.id: Sangat panas, tapi kita bisa keluar.

pairs.en: It's too hot to go out.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Budi worked at the office until 2 a.m. Can he drive home safely?

question.prompt: Complete: He was ___ tired to drive home, so he took an ojek.
question.explanation: There's a problem: he can't drive. **too** + adjective + **to** + verb: **too tired to drive**. *very* only describes, so it can't take *to drive* like this. *too much* goes before uncountable nouns (*too much work*), not before an adjective.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina tastes her mother's rendang. She loves it!

options: This rendang is too much delicious!
question.explanation: **so** adds feeling and praise: **so delicious** = *enak banget*. **too** always means a problem, so *too delicious* sounds like a complaint, even if *terlalu enak* is praise in Indonesian. *too much* never goes before an adjective.

steps.title: enough: after describing words
steps.text: Last one: enough, and the trap in Indonesian cukup.
steps.body:
**enough** (say 'i-NAF') = *cukup*, as much as you need. It goes **after** an adjective or adverb: *old enough to vote*. Negative: **not … enough**: *The bag isn't big enough.* Before a **noun** it comes first: *enough money*. Two patterns: after describing words, before thing words.

Trap: *cukup besar* puts cukup first, so people say `enough big`. And *cukup* can mean **quite** (*lumayan*): *quite big* = lumayan besar; *big enough* = sesuai kebutuhan.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Sari's old laptop needs five minutes to open one file.

question.prompt: Complete: It isn't ___ for her work.
question.explanation: **enough** goes after the describing word: **fast enough**. `enough fast` copies the Indonesian order (*cukup cepat*). *too fast* would mean it's very fast, the opposite of her problem.

steps.text: Here is the whole lesson on one page.

examples.en: It was such a good film that I watched it twice.
examples.id: Filmnya begitu bagus sehingga saya menontonnya dua kali.

This table isn't big enough for eight people.

id.greeting: Halo! Hari ini kamu akan belajar mengatakan seberapa kuat sebuah sifat, dan apa akibatnya: so hot, such a good film, too tired, old enough. Yuk kita pelajari langkah demi langkah.

steps.title: so + kata sifat
steps.text: Kamu sudah kenal very, really dan quite. Kita mulai dengan kata yang menambah perasaan: so.
steps.body:
**so** membuat kata lebih kuat, dengan perasaan, mirip *banget*: *It's so hot today!* (Panas banget hari ini!) Letaknya sebelum **kata sifat** (adjective, kata yang menjelaskan: *hot, tired*) atau **adverb** (cara: *fast, well*), **tanpa kata benda** setelahnya.

Tambahkan **that** + apa yang terjadi untuk menunjukkan **akibat**: *I was so tired that I fell asleep on the KRL.* Dalam bahasa Indonesia: *begitu … sehingga …*. Ini bukan *so* = *jadi* dari kata penghubung (*I was tired, so I went home*).

pairs.en: I was so tired that I fell asleep on the KRL.
pairs.id: Saya begitu capek sehingga tertidur di KRL.

steps.title: such + frasa kata benda
steps.text: Sekarang, bagaimana kalau ada kata benda di akhir?
steps.body:
Kalau frasanya **berakhir dengan kata benda** (noun, kata untuk benda atau orang: *film, beaches, weather*), pakai **such**. Satu benda yang bisa dihitung → **such a/an**: *such a good film*. Jamak atau tak terhitung → **such** tanpa a: *such long queues, such bad weather*.

Tes cepat: lihat **kata terakhir**. Kata sifat → **so**; kata benda → **such**. Bukan `so a good film`.

examples.en: It was such a good film!
Pak Hasan is such a patient boss.
examples.id: Pak Hasan atasan yang sabar sekali.
Bali punya pantai-pantai yang indah sekali.

examples.en: We had such bad weather in Puncak.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rekan kerja baru Sari membantunya setiap hari. Lihat kata terakhir frasanya.

question.explanation: Frasanya berakhir dengan kata benda (**people**), jadi pakai **such**. *people* itu jamak, jadi tanpa *a*: **such nice people**. `so nice people` salah: so tidak bisa ada sebelum frasa kata benda.

steps.title: Susun kalimat
steps.text: Kemarin ada badai besar di Bogor. Ceritakan apa akibatnya.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Hujannya begitu deras sehingga kami tinggal di rumah.
question.solution: It rained so hard that we stayed home.
question.explanation: **so** + adverb (*rain hard* = hujan deras), lalu **that** + akibatnya: *we stayed home*. *begitu … sehingga* = **so … that**.

steps.title: too = masalah
steps.text: Berikutnya: kata yang selalu berarti ada masalah.
steps.body:
**too** = *terlalu*: lebih dari yang wajar. *This shirt is too small* (tidak bisa saya pakai). Tambahkan **to + kata kerja** untuk hal yang tidak bisa dilakukan: *He's too young to vote*, atau **for** + orang: *too expensive for me*.

Sebelum kata sifat cukup **too** saja, bukan `too much expensive`: **too much** dipakai sebelum kata benda tak terhitung (*too much sugar*).

Jebakan: *terlalu enak* bisa jadi pujian dalam bahasa Indonesia, tapi **too** dalam bahasa Inggris tidak pernah. Untuk memuji pakai **so / really / very**.

pairs.en: It's very hot, but we can go out.
pairs.id: Sangat panas, tapi kita bisa keluar.

pairs.en: It's too hot to go out.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Budi bekerja di kantor sampai jam 2 pagi. Bisakah dia menyetir pulang dengan aman?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: He was ___ tired to drive home, so he took an ojek.
question.explanation: Ada masalah: dia tidak bisa menyetir. **too** + kata sifat + **to** + kata kerja: **too tired to drive**. *very* hanya menjelaskan, jadi tidak bisa diikuti *to drive* seperti ini. *too much* dipakai sebelum kata benda tak terhitung (*too much work*), bukan sebelum kata sifat.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina mencicipi rendang buatan ibunya. Dia suka sekali!

options: This rendang is too much delicious!
question.explanation: **so** menambah perasaan dan pujian: **so delicious** = *enak banget*. **too** selalu berarti masalah, jadi *too delicious* terdengar seperti keluhan, walaupun *terlalu enak* bisa jadi pujian dalam bahasa Indonesia. *too much* tidak pernah ada sebelum kata sifat.

steps.title: enough: setelah kata sifat
steps.text: Yang terakhir: enough, dan jebakan kata cukup.
steps.body:
**enough** (dibaca 'i-NAF') = *cukup*, sebanyak yang dibutuhkan. Letaknya **setelah** kata sifat atau adverb: *old enough to vote*. Negatif: **not … enough**: *The bag isn't big enough.* Sebelum **kata benda**, enough di depan: *enough money*. Dua pola: setelah kata sifat, sebelum kata benda.

Jebakan: *cukup besar* menaruh cukup di depan, jadi orang bilang `enough big`. Dan *cukup* bisa berarti **quite** (*lumayan*): *quite big* = lumayan besar; *big enough* = sesuai kebutuhan.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Laptop lama Sari butuh lima menit untuk membuka satu file.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: It isn't ___ for her work.
question.explanation: **enough** ada setelah kata sifat: **fast enough**. `enough fast` meniru urutan bahasa Indonesia (*cukup cepat*). *too fast* berarti laptopnya sangat cepat, kebalikan dari masalahnya.
